name: What are the most common modifications in an accessible bathroom renovation?

mainEntity.name: What are the most common modifications in an accessible bathroom renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common accessible bathroom modifications include converting standard tubs into zero-threshold roll-in showers, widening doorways for mobility equipment, and mounting heavy-duty grab bars. Homeowners also frequently add slip-resistant tile flooring, comfort-height toilets, and roll-under floating vanities. HH Remodeling handles the finish carpentry, framing adjustments, drywall patching, and custom tile installation directly, while coordinating licensed sub-trades to relocate plumbing valves or adjust electrical switches to reachable heights. These changes remove physical trip hazards while keeping the bathroom functional for the entire household.
acceptedAnswer.description: Accessible bathroom remodels typically include roll-in tile showers, widened doorways, reinforced grab bars, comfort-height toilets, and open-front roll-under vanities.
